rounds.text: Umiya Tubes Ltd trades at an attractive valuation, featuring a P/E of 12.7x and a price-to-book ratio of 1.37x against a book value of ₹20.0 [E1, E2]. These multiples sit at a clear discount to sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E is 25.04x and the P/B is 2.37x [E6, E7]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow valuation estimates intrinsic value at ₹88 per share, which leaves a substantial margin of safety of 68.9% [E43, E44]. The reverse DCF indicates that the current market price of ₹27.4 only implies a modest 1.9% earnings growth, whereas the base case assumes 18.0% [E2, E45]. Fundamental momentum is robust, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 2615% and profit growth of 203% [E17, E21]. The company is exceptionally well-financed, boasting a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and zero borrowings as of March 2026 [E37, E38]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped significantly to 3.33% [E40], and operating cash flow for March 2026 is negative at Rs -18.03 Cr [E34].

Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 12.7x and a price-to-book of 1.37x [E1, E2], and features zero borrowings of Rs 0.00 Cr in March 2026 [E38]. However, those low valuation multiples and the proposed DCF intrinsic value of ₹88 [E43] ignore the catastrophic collapse in promoter ownership from 49.98% in September 2023 down to a negligible 3.33% by June 2026 [E40], signaling a complete abandonment by insiders. While the bull highlights staggering TTM sales growth of 2615% [E17], this explosive top-line expansion completely failed to generate cash, resulting in a disastrous negative operating cash flow and free cash flow of Rs -18.03 Cr for March 2026 [E34, E35]. This cash drain creates a horrible cash conversion ratio of -6.44x against reported profit [E33], meaning the massive earnings touted by the bull are entirely unbacked by actual cash generation. Furthermore, the company suffers from severely bloated debtors stretching to 224 days [E62], exposing severe receivables risk behind those paper profits. Finally, despite the theoretical margin of safety [E44], the stock languishes below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a lagging relative-strength rating of just 21 [E48, E49] and a terrifying historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -95.2% [E51].
